title: Shell in Go
summary: A POSIX-inspired command-line shell, implementing command parsing, pipelines, process execution and job control.

diagram.description: Input is tokenised by the parser, assembled into a pipeline, then executed as built-in commands or external processes.

capabilities: Built-in commands and external program execution.
Multi-command pipelines and stdout/stderr redirection.
Quoting, escaping and parameter expansion.
Tab completion, background jobs and persistent history.
organization: Separate packages for parsing, commands, pipelines, completion and shell state.

sections.title: Project context
paragraphs: Built as a learning project to explore how a shell parses input, connects processes and manages state. The repository demonstrates these capabilities; it does not claim full POSIX compliance.

note: Learning project · CodeCrafters Build Your Own Shell

title: Rutuliukai
summary: A static browser arena survival game. Dodge enemies, level up, and build a loadout to survive the next wave.

diagram.description: GitHub Pages serves the static game. The browser loads the gameplay data and runs the game on an HTML canvas.

stages.label: Browser game
stages.caption: Run the game and render the arena

capabilities: Canvas-based combat with automatic weapons and keyboard-controlled abilities.
Choose upgrades as you level up and equip abilities in the shop.
Review run statistics and save your best kill count in the browser.
organization: The static HTML entry point loads the game code from src and gameplay settings, shop items, and upgrades from data.

title: Quiz
summary: A lightweight browser quiz with category-based question sets.

diagram.description: Select a category, load its JSON question bank, display questions and answer choices, and update the scorecard.

capabilities: Category selection and separate question banks.
Question rendering and answer-choice handling.
Quiz navigation and score display.
England, general knowledge and India question data.
organization: Separate modules for state, categories, questions, quiz flow and scoring, plus shared event and DOM utilities.

title: Portfolio Website
summary: This static portfolio showcases my engineering experience, certifications, and projects.

diagram.description: Vite bundles the React app and its JSON content. GitHub Pages serves the build, and React renders the selected page in the browser.

stages.label: Vite build
stages.caption: Bundle the app and JSON content

capabilities: Browse projects by engineering category and share links to individual project pages.
Publish the site as static files with GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.
organization: React features live in src/features, portfolio content in src/data, and images in public.

title: LLM Coding Assistant
summary: A local coding assistant with an agent loop and tool calling.

diagram.description: A prompt is sent to the model. The model can call local tools and receive their results repeatedly. Once no further tool calls are needed, the model returns its final response.

capabilities: OpenAI-compatible model integration.
Agent loop retaining messages and tool results.
Tools for command execution and file read/write.
Registered tool definitions and dispatch by name.
organization: Separate agent, configuration and tool packages, with implementations for shell execution and file operations.

title: Obsidian RAG
summary: A local RAG API for searching Obsidian notes and generating answers with source citations.

diagram.description: Notes are chunked, embedded and indexed in pgvector. Questions use similarity or MMR search. /retrieve returns passages directly; /ask uses an LLM to generate an answer with sources.

stages.label: Similarity or MMR
stages.caption: Find relevant passages or balance relevance and diversity

stages.label: /ask · LLM
stages.caption: Generate an answer from retrieved passages

stages.label: API response
stages.caption: /retrieve: passages and distances · /ask: answer and sources

capabilities: Index Markdown notes without modifying the vault.
Similarity and MMR search over a persistent vector index.
Retrieve source passages or generate answers with citations.
Local LLM inference and incremental re-indexing.
organization: Separate modules for note loading, embeddings, storage, retrieval and answer generation, exposed through FastAPI endpoints.
